events.title: Simula 67 classes presented at IFIP
events.summary: Dahl and Nygaard presented class and subclass declarations at the IFIP Working Conference on Simulation Languages in Oslo.
events.about: Simula 67 introduced objects, classes, inheritance, and late binding — the concepts behind object-oriented programming. Originally built for discrete-event simulation (queues, factories, traffic), it became the direct ancestor of C++, Smalltalk, Java, and Python's class model.

narrative.whyChosen: This is the birth moment of object-oriented programming as a language feature, not just a design pattern.
narrative.whyImportant: Classes unified data and behavior; inheritance let models share structure — ideas every modern language copied.
narrative.problemSolved: Simulation programs needed reusable, composable models of real-world entities without duplicating code for each scenario.

sources.title: Dahl — The Birth of Object Orientation: the Simula Languages (IFIP May 1967)
